headline: Haida Gwaii Orientation and Gwaii Haanas Entry
reservation: Visitors to Gwaii Haanas National Park Reserve must complete a mandatory orientation session and obtain a permit before entry. Accommodation in Queen Charlotte and Masset is limited and should be secured well in advance of the summer season. Different rules apply for independent travelers versus those using licensed tour operators.

days.title: Graham Island Heritage

stops.name: Haida Heritage Centre at Kay Llnagaay
stops.detail: Learn about the living culture of the Haida people through totem poles and traditional longhouses.

stops.name: Balance Rock
stops.detail: Visit this glacial erratic positioned precariously on the shoreline just north of Skidegate.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for local road travel; conditions vary with weather.
days.note: Respect local cultural protocols and stay on designated paths at heritage sites.

days.title: Naikoon Wilderness

stops.name: Tow Hill
stops.detail: Hike the boardwalk to the summit for views over the Dixon Entrance and the expansive North Beach.

stops.name: Rose Spit
stops.detail: A significant ecological site where the Hecate Strait and Dixon Entrance meet; check tide tables for beach access.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours for the drive from Masset to the Tow Hill area on unpaved sections.
days.note: Beach driving requires specific experience and vehicle capabilities; check local conditions.

days.title: Southern Moresby Exploration

stops.name: Moresby Camp
stops.detail: The primary staging area for boat trips into the Gwaii Haanas wilderness area.

stops.name: Skidegate Inlet
stops.detail: Observe the marine life and rugged coastline while transiting between the two main islands.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours for the drive to Moresby Camp; check active logging road status.
days.note: Industrial traffic has the right of way on all gravel access roads.

intel.title: Heritage Site and Trailhead Access
intel.text: Designated parking is available at the Haida Heritage Centre and Tow Hill. Do not block access roads used by local residents or forestry vehicles.

intel.title: Remote Communication Realities
intel.text: Reliable signal is limited to the main hubs of Masset, Skidegate, and Queen Charlotte. Expect no service once traveling into Naikoon or Gwaii Haanas.

intel.title: Gateway Fuel Stations
intel.text: Refuel in Masset or Queen Charlotte City before heading to remote trailheads. Sandspit has fuel, but hours vary; always carry a reserve if exploring backroads.

intel.title: Tidal Timing Constraints
intel.text: Many coastal walks and beach access points are only traversable at low tide. Consult local tide tables daily to avoid being cut off by rising waters.

intel.title: Logging Road Protocols
intel.text: Travel to Moresby Camp involves gravel roads shared with logging trucks. Use headlights and yield to industrial traffic at all times.

plan.arrival: Fly into Sandspit (YZP), take the Alliford Bay ferry to Skidegate, and pick up a vehicle in Queen Charlotte City.
plan.vehicle: A 4WD vehicle with high clearance is recommended for exploring Naikoon and Moresby Island logging roads; check rental contracts for gravel road exclusions.
plan.goldenHour: Sunset at North Beach near Tow Hill, with views across to Alaska on clear summer evenings.
